knowledge_gaps: Fault detection is not operationally defined: the report needs a mutation-to-probe table, exact severities, tolerances, denominators and expected responses. Residual suppression is an intervention without a universally correct ranking response.

The proposed future-dependence mutation must depend on the perturbed future token and run through the existing causal probe. Directly changing a feature and checking that same feature risks a circular test.

Reproducibility requires exact hook locations, residual-branch boundaries, candidate eligibility, selection rules and exception-safe cleanup. Restoring RNG states alone may not restore a consumed training-loader sampler or worker state.

The report shifts from candidate-depth calibration to fault testing without explaining which candidate-depth estimators it will validate. Nested-rank monotonicity, exact-rank agreement and hypergeometric expectations need explicit checks.

Originality 4/10 is plausible for an adaptation, but potential 7/10 lacks prospective evidence and difficulty 4/10 may underestimate safe integration. References need verified titles, authors and supporting passages; the twenty-user full-catalog feedback workflow also needs an explicit place in the design.

follow_up_queries.reason: Establish independent detection criteria and avoid optimizing the diagnostic suite only for its own synthetic faults.
follow_up_queries.query: In metamorphic and mutation testing of neural sequential recommenders, how are independent test oracles, equivalent or ineffective mutants, held-out mutation operators and mutation-score denominators defined? Examine the studies at DOI 10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410 and DOI 10.1016/j.infsof.2025.107807, verify their bibliographic details, and assess which findings support a NextItNet audit using incorrect left-padding readout, future-token leakage and residual-branch suppression.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve implementation risks that could invalidate causality checks or alter subsequent training despite unchanged weights.
follow_up_queries.query: For PyTorch residual dilated causal convolution networks such as NextItNet, what implementation practices support reversible forward-hook fault injection and future-token causality tests? Address injecting an actual dependency on a perturbed future embedding, preserving residual skip paths, cloning hooked outputs, removing temporary hooks after exceptions, restoring per-module modes and buffers, and avoiding changes to DataLoader sampler and worker RNG state.

follow_up_queries.reason: Reconnect fault calibration to the original candidate-depth research question using analytical checks that require no additional fitted model.
follow_up_queries.query: For recommender evaluation with one fixed positive and m unique uniformly sampled negatives without replacement from N eligible negatives, how can sampled HR@10 and expected rank be validated against the positive's exact eligible-pool rank? Investigate hypergeometric expectations, deterministic tie handling, nested-candidate rank monotonicity, common-user paired comparisons and Monte Carlo uncertainty, including 'On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems' and subsequent sampled-metric research.
